attempts.systemPrompt:
Trip shape: resort
Specialist: lodging

You are the lodging specialist on a trip-planning tool.
You propose places to sleep that match the roughest night the party said they would accept, and you say how far ahead each one has to be booked. A proposal does one of two things. It names one premises, an establishment or a site, by its name and at its locality: `place.name` is that name and `place.locality` the town. Or it says plainly, in its title or its summary, that it is a kind of place and names no premises: then `place.name` holds the kind, for example `motel`, and `place.locality` the town. Where you are given places to stay from map data for a town, a premises you name there is one of those, under the name it is given, if any of them fits the party. A kind of place is the fallback, for a town whose list is empty or where nothing in it fits.

You propose options. You never write a schedule: nothing you return says which day it falls on, what order things happen in, or what time anything starts. Another part of this tool packs the days, in code.

Rules, and they are not negotiable:
- Reply with JSON and nothing else, in exactly this shape:
{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "title": "short, and never an itinerary",
      "summary": "why this is worth doing, in a sentence or two",
      "location": { "kind": "at", "place": { "name": "...", "locality": "... or null", "coordinates": null } },
      "durationMinutes": 0,
      "cost": { "currency": "ISO-4217", "low": 0, "high": 0, "basis": "per-person | per-party", "provenance": { "kind": "model-asserted" } },
      "season": { "from": "MM-DD", "to": "MM-DD" },
      "bookingLeadTimeDays": 0
    }
  ]
}
- At most 6 candidates. Fewer is a fine answer; an empty list is a fine answer.
- Anything you do not know is null. A duration nobody measured is null, not a plausible ninety minutes. A season nobody checked is null — which is not the same as all year, and all year is written {"from":"01-01","to":"12-31"}.
- Costs are bands with a currency and a basis, never a single figure and never a quote. Do not total anything.
- A slot that says "not answered" is unknown to you. Say in the summary what you could not account for, and propose anyway. Never invent the answer and never refuse to propose.
- Never book anything, never ask for payment details, and never present what you write as clearance to go anywhere.
- Every candidate is at one place, so its location is {"kind":"at","place":{...}}.
- This trip has 8 days.

candidatesAccepted.summary: Every Canadian flying to a typical beach all-inclusive (Caribbean or Mexico) needs their own valid passport, the 2-year-old included. Many destinations also want six months' validity. The destination is not answered, so confirm the exact entry rules once it is chosen. Child passports can take weeks to arrive.

candidatesAccepted.title: Out-of-country medical and trip-cancellation insurance
candidatesAccepted.summary: Provincial health coverage pays very little abroad. A family policy covering emergency medical care and cancellation protects a 7,000 CAD trip with three young children. Destination and access needs are not answered, so check the policy wording against both once they are known.

candidatesAccepted.title: Consent letter if one parent travels alone with the children
candidatesAccepted.summary: Canada recommends a signed consent letter whenever children travel without both parents, and some destinations ask for one at the border. It is only needed if the adults travel separately at any point. Bring the children's birth certificates as backup either way.

place.name: Home, or a notary if the destination asks for a witnessed letter

candidatesAccepted.title: Roaming plan or eSIM for staying reachable at the resort
candidatesAccepted.summary: Resort wifi can be patchy across beach properties. A carrier travel pack or an eSIM keeps the adults reachable while the 6-year-old is at the kids' club, with no need to leave the property. The destination is not answered, so check coverage there before buying.

candidatesAccepted.title: Family all-inclusive beach resort, Riviera Maya
candidatesAccepted.summary: A nonstop from Ottawa to Cancún avoids the connection rule. Many all-inclusives here have splash pools and kids' clubs from age 4, so nobody needs to leave the property. The band assumes one family room or two connecting rooms, 7 nights all-inclusive, for 5 people. It does not include flights, which are shown separately. Access needs were not answered and are not accounted for. Check the pool depth and kids' club ages with the specific property.

candidatesAccepted.title: Return flights Ottawa–Cancún, nonstop or one short connection
candidatesAccepted.summary: Seasonal nonstops from Ottawa are typical in winter. Otherwise it needs one connection under two hours, usually via Toronto or Montreal. This is a fare band per seat. The two-year-old usually needs a paid seat on international flights, and lap-infant rules vary by airline. Taxes are assumed included, and checked bags are not.

candidatesAccepted.title: Family all-inclusive beach resort, Punta Cana
candidatesAccepted.summary: This is an alternative to Mexico. Punta Cana is widely served by winter flights from Ottawa, and many resorts there have kids' clubs and shallow pools. The band assumes a family suite, 7 nights all-inclusive, for 5 people, and excludes flights. Access needs are not accounted for. The pool depth for a two-year-old should be confirmed per property.

place.name: Punta Cana / Bávaro all-inclusive resort zone

candidatesAccepted.title: Pre-arranged resort airport transfer
candidatesAccepted.summary: A shared or private shuttle between the airport and the resort means no car rental and nothing to organise on landing. The band is per party for a return trip and assumes a van sized for 5 with a child seat on request.
